info.title: daylight_server
info.summary: GPU daylight, solar and view analysis on meshes, over HTTP.
info.description:
Runs both tools of [kit-sim_core](https://github.com/Cybernaut0815/kit-sim_core) on uploaded meshes for several users at once: `daylight` (radiation, illuminance and sun hours over a year, a period or an instant; OptiX ray tracing, Perez sky, validated against Ladybug Tools, Radiance and pvlib) and `views` (what each element sees: sky, ground, obstruction and target shares, distances, isovists). One GPU worker runs queued jobs in turn; uploads, validation, cached answers and polls never wait for it.

## Workflow

1. **Upload each mesh once**: `PUT /mesh/{id}` with a `.dmesh` image under an id you choose (content ids make equal meshes upload nothing; `POST /meshes/missing` says which to send).
2. **Submit**: `POST /jobs` (multipart, `RunRequest`): receiving meshes in `sensors`, shading-only ones in `context`, the tool's CLI flags in `args` (`GET /usage/{tool}` lists them), weather as `epw`, `epw_url` or `--clear-sky` (views takes none). A `404 {missing}` lists the ids to upload before submitting again.
3. **Wait**: `GET /jobs/{id}?wait=25` (long poll) while `state` is `queued` or `running`.
4. **Read** when `done`: `getJobValues` streams the values (float32, column-major), `inline=1` adds them as `values_b64`. Rows follow `meshes[]` (`first`, `count`): one per face, or per point with `--on vertices`.
5. **Cancel** with `DELETE /jobs/{id}` when the result is no longer needed.

`POST /run` does steps 2 to 4 in one blocking call.

## Example

```sh
curl -T box.dmesh "http://localhost:8080/mesh/3f1c0b9e-0d59-4a8e-9a43-1b7a6a0c2e11?name=roof"
curl -F sensors=3f1c0b9e-0d59-4a8e-9a43-1b7a6a0c2e11 -F args=--lat -F args=52.52 -F args=--lon -F args=13.41 -F args=--tz -F args=1 \
     -F args=--quantity -F args=radiation,sunhours -F args=--clear-sky http://localhost:8080/jobs
curl "http://localhost:8080/jobs/<id from the answer>?wait=25"
```

Decoding `values_b64` (float64 little-endian, row-major): Python `numpy.frombuffer(base64.b64decode(r['values_b64']), '<f8').reshape(-1, len(r['columns']))`, JavaScript `new Float64Array(Uint8Array.from(atob(r.values_b64), c => c.charCodeAt(0)).buffer)`.

## Units

`.dmesh` coordinates are metres, Z up, right-handed winding (the normal points to the front side). Daylight: `radiation`, `direct`, `diffuse` kWh/m² over the period, `irradiance` W/m² mean, `illuminance` lux mean, `sunhours` hours. Views: shares 0..1, distances m, `volume` m³. Columns are `<quantity>_<side>` (`radiation_front`). Surfaces are opaque and black unless `--optics`, `--transmission on` and `--bounces` say otherwise.

## Errors and limits

Errors are `text/plain` (`ErrorText`); a usage error is a `400` with the CLI usage appended. Names in `--optics`, `--no-occlude` and `--target` are resolved when the job runs (an `error` job, status 500). `429`: this client has `--client-jobs` (default 2) jobs queued or running (the `X-Client-Id` header names a client, else its network address); `503`: the queue holds `--max-queue` (default 32). Both carry `Retry-After`. Finished jobs are kept 15 minutes. No authentication: job ids are random UUIDs only their submitter knows.

## Web app and agents

`/sets` stores the web app's analysis sets and combined views for every client. With `--mcp`, agents on this machine drive the app over MCP (`mcpMessage`, tag `agents`); the other `agents` routes serve the app.

put.description:
Stores one mesh in the server's RAM cache under your id, replacing one stored before (the least recently used are evicted when the cache is full: a job naming an evicted id gets `404 {missing}`). The body is one `.dmesh` image, little-endian, no padding:

| offset | type | content |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | char[4] | `DLM1` |
| 4 | uint32 | flags: bit 0 = a slot block follows the indices; other bits 0 |
| 8 | uint64 | n_points |
| 16 | uint64 | n_faces |
| 24 | uint64 | n_indices |
| 32 | float64[3 n_points] | xyz, metres, Z up |
| | int32[n_faces] | vertices per face (>= 3), right-handed winding |
| | int32[n_indices] | 0-based point indices, sum(counts) = n_indices |
| | uint16[n_faces] | flags bit 0 only: each face's optics slot (`--optics NAME/SLOT=...`; without the block all are slot 0) |

Another flag bit or a short slot block is a `400`. The bindings write it: `toDmesh(mesh)` (TypeScript), `daylight.to_dmesh(...)` (Python).

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Display name, echoed in `meshes[].name` and the NAME that `--optics`, `--no-occlude` and `--target` address: sanitised to `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`, made unique per run ignoring case (a second `roof` is `roof_2`). Defaults to the id.

get.summary: Check whether a mesh is cached
get.description: Answers 204 when the server holds the mesh, 404 when it must be uploaded (again).

post.summary: Which mesh ids the server lacks
post.description: One call before uploading a model: the ids (for example content hashes of the .dmesh bytes) the server does not hold, in request order; upload only those with `uploadMesh`. The ids it holds count as used for its mesh cache (LRU), so they stay for the run that follows.

Validates the request at once (bad flags, unknown mesh ids, unusable weather fail here) and queues the run for the GPU. Answers the job: `202` while queued, or `200` with a finished job when an identical request was answered before (same mesh ids, args and weather; `cache.response` is then `hit`). Follow it with `GET /jobs/{id}?wait=25`.

200.description: Answered from the result cache: the job is already `done`.

get.summary: Queue overview and this client's jobs
get.description: How busy the GPU is, and the jobs submitted by this client (same `X-Client-Id`, else the same network address). Other clients' job ids are never listed.

get.summary: Get a job, optionally waiting for a change
get.description: The job's state and queue position. When `done` it carries the result fields (`columns`, `meshes`, `rows`, `cols`, and `values`: where `getJobValues` serves them; `values_b64` only with `inline=1`), when `error` or `cancelled` the message and `status`. With `wait=S` it returns as soon as the state or the position changes, at the latest after S seconds.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: Seconds to wait for a change, 0 to 30.

delete.description: A queued job leaves the queue at once (`cancelled`); a running one stops at its next trace chunk (still `running` in this answer, `cancelled` shortly after). A finished job is returned unchanged.

get.description: The values of a `done` job as raw float32 little-endian, column-major: column 0 for every row (rows = `sum(meshes.count)`, in `meshes` order), then column 1, and so on; `Content-Length` = rows x cols x 4. With `col=k` only column k. Streamed, and `Range` requests work. Results are kept as long as their job: `--job-ttl-min`, and the oldest go first past `--results-mb`.

409.description: The job is not `done` (queued, running, error or cancelled).

post.description: Submits like `submitJob` and keeps the request open until the job finishes, then answers the result object directly (the same fields a `done` job carries, without the job fields). Simple for scripts; for long runs or a progress display use `submitJob` + `getJob`.

409.description: Cancelled while it ran (`DELETE /jobs/{id}` from another request).

500.description: The run failed: a runtime error from the core, or a name in `--optics`, `--no-occlude` or `--target` that the run's meshes do not resolve (unknown, ambiguous, a context mesh, a slot it lacks, a row given twice).

optics.value: error: --optics roof/3: slot out of range (the mesh has slots 0..1)

507.description: Out of host or GPU memory for this run; the server keeps running. Use fewer receivers or quantities.

text/plain.example: error: out of memory: the server ran out of host memory for this run (17244108 rows x 6 columns; 1.3 GB RAM free, 2.1 GB commit free now)

get.summary: Download a weather resource through the server cache
get.description:
Fetches an allowed public weather resource once and serves it from disk afterwards (browsers cannot fetch them: no CORS). The same URLs work as `epw_url`. Allowed prefixes:

- `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NREL/EnergyPlus/develop/weather/master.geojson`: the EnergyPlus station index (GeoJSON; each feature's `properties.epw` is an anchor whose `href` is the station's EPW)
- `https://energyplus-weather.s3.amazonaws.com/`: EnergyPlus weather files
- `https://re.jrc.ec.europa.eu/api/v5_3/tmy?`: PVGIS typical year for any location, e.g. `...tmy?lat=52.52&lon=13.41&outputformat=epw`

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: The resource URL, URL-encoded (its own `&` must not split the query).

get.description: Every set and combined view stored with `saveSet`, each as a JSON string (parsed one by one, so a damaged file cannot break the list), from `<cache>/sets/<id>.json` (`--cache`, default `%LOCALAPPDATA%\daylight_server`). Every client sees the same list; agents reach it through the app's set tools (`app_state` lists them).

put.summary: Store an analysis set or combined view (app)
put.description: Creates or replaces `<id>.json` with the body (at most 256 KB): an `AnalysisSet` or a `CombinedView`, stored as it comes (written to a temporary file and renamed, so a crash never leaves half a set). At most 500 sets; no owner or version check: the last write wins.

409.description: A new set while 500 are stored.

delete.summary: Delete an analysis set or combined view (app)
delete.description: Removes `<id>.json`. Combined views that use a deleted set show it as missing.

get.description: Liveness, the GPU, and how busy the queue is.

The `daylight` or `views` CLI's `-h` text, the one list of the flags a job's `args` take: grouped by topic, with values, defaults and examples. `RunRequest.args` names the ones refused over HTTP.

post.description:
The web app's MCP server for agents on this machine (Claude Code, Claude Desktop). It answers the handshake and `tools/list` itself and relays each `tools/call` to the app open in a browser tab (`bridgeNext`), which carries it out live. With no tab open it starts the app hidden in headless Chrome (`--web` or `--app-url`); an app tab opened later picks that session up.

## Protocol

MCP Streamable HTTP, revisions 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18 and 2025-03-26 (the ones with `initialize`). One JSON-RPC message per POST, answered as `application/json`: no SSE (`mcpGet` answers 405), no `Mcp-Session-Id`, no batches, prompts or resources.

| message | answer |
|---|---|
| `initialize` | `protocolVersion` (the one asked for when supported, else `2025-11-25`), `capabilities: {tools: {}}`, `serverInfo`, `instructions` |
| `ping` | `{}` |
| `tools/list` | every tool, one page |
| `tools/call` | the app's `CallToolResult` |
| a notification (no `id`) | `202`; `notifications/cancelled` cancels the call |
| anything else | error `-32601` |

JSON-RPC errors come with HTTP 200 and echo the request's `id` (`-32602`: an unknown tool). **Every call answers within 55 s** (Claude Desktop ends tool calls at about 60 s): a long step (a run, a big model, a PDF) goes on in the app and the reply says `running` or `generating`, so call again. No app tab, or no answer within 55 s, is an `isError` result that says what to do.

## Connect

Start `daylight_server --web ..\web\dist --mcp`, then:

- **Claude Code**: `claude mcp add --transport http daylight http://127.0.0.1:8080/mcp` (if it does not connect, start it with `MCP_PROTOCOL_NEGOTIATION=legacy`).
- **Claude Desktop** (stdio only): merge the entry below into `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json` with absolute paths (`where node`) and restart it. `server/mcp-stdio.mjs` (Node 18+, no packages) relays to `http://127.0.0.1:8080/mcp`; a URL after the script picks another address.

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "daylight": { "command": "C:\\Program Files\\nodejs\\node.exe", "args": ["F:\\Github\\kit-sim_daylight_frontend\\server\\mcp-stdio.mjs"] } } }
```

## Tools

Models by letter A-D, parts by USD prim path, times in local standard time; `tools/list` has each tool's schema, `guide` the workflows.

- **State and knowledge:** `app_state` (first), `guide`, `site_info`
- **Models:** `open_model`, `remove_model`, `model_tree`, `set_roles`, `set_visibility`, `set_geometry`, `get_materials`, `edit_material`, `update_settings`
- **Runs and results:** `run`, `results`, `find_critical`, `download_result`
- **Views:** `set_display`, `set_camera`, `save_view`, `screenshot`
- **Reports:** `get_report`, `save_report`, `delete_report`, `generate_report`
- **Sets and combined views:** `save_set`, `open_set`, `copy_set`, `rename_set`, `run_set`, `delete_set`, `save_combined` (`results` quotes a set's kept results and a combined view; `rename_set` and `delete_set` take either kind)

parameters.name: MCP-Protocol-Version
parameters.description: The revision agreed in `initialize`, which clients send on every later request.

200.description: The JSON-RPC answer: the method's `result`, or an `error` (`-32601` unknown method, `-32602` no or an unknown tool name). A tool that could not do its step answers `isError: true` and a text saying what to do.

result.instructions: This server drives the daylight app in the user's browser tab ... Start with app_state.

content.text: No daylight app tab is open on this machine: ask the user to open the app and keep its tab open (LAN tabs cannot be driven), or to start daylight_server with --web or --app-url so it can start a hidden instance itself.

202.description: A notification (no `id`, e.g. `notifications/initialized`): accepted, no body.

400.description: Not a message this server takes: an `MCP-Protocol-Version` header naming another revision on a request other than `initialize` (`text/plain`; a newer client then falls back to `initialize`), a body that is not one JSON object (`-32700`), or a batch, a body without a `method`, or an `id` that is neither string nor number (`-32600`).

error.message: Parse error: the body is not one JSON object

get.description: MCP lets a server offer a `GET` stream for messages to the client; this one opens none (no SSE, no sessions), so `GET /mcp` answers `405` with `Allow: POST`. Send every message with `mcpMessage`.

get.summary: Next tool call for an app tab (long poll)
get.description: The web app's side of the relay; agents do not call it. Each page load keeps one `wait=25` poll open, gets the next `tools/call` meant for it and answers with `bridgeResult`; `wait=0` is a ping that keeps the tab live (with `focus=1`: the one the user looked at last). A call goes to a live tab (a poll open, or seen within 5 s): the user's tabs before the hidden instance (`kind=headless`), then the one focused last, then the one seen last. With none, a tab gets 5 s to come back, then the server starts the hidden instance (`--web` or `--app-url`) and gives it 30 s to poll (started again after a minute without one). A poll from a user's tab ends a hidden instance that has no session to hand over and no call on its way. Tabs gone for a minute are forgotten.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: Seconds to wait for a call, 0 to 25; 0 is a ping.

parameters.name: focus
parameters.description: `1` when the page's window has focus.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: `headless` from the hidden instance; the user's tabs leave it out.

200.description: A call for this tab: its id and the `tools/call` params, raw (`arguments` added as `{}` when the agent left it out).

204.description: No call within `wait` seconds, or a ping.

post.description: The tab's answer to a call from `bridgeNext`: one MCP `CallToolResult` object, sent as `Content-Type: application/json` and passed to the agent unchanged as the `tools/call` result.

content.text: {"view":{...},"description":"seen from the S (180°), 20° above the horizon, 42 m away"}

404.description: No such call (answered already, past its 55 s, or the agent hung up), or agent routes are off.

get.summary: Read a model file or folder on this machine (app tab)
get.description: How the app opens a model by path (`open_model`): a file's bytes, or a folder's model files listed recursively for the tab to fetch. Absolute drive-letter paths only (no network share or device path) and only model, texture and weather files (`.usd .usda .usdc .usdz .glb .gltf .obj .mtl .bin .png .jpg .jpeg .webp .exr .hdr .epw`), each checked as the file it opens (a symlink's target, a short name's long name) and at most `--max-mb`. A listing skips other files, dot names, `__MACOSX` and links, and holds at most 2000 files and `--max-mb` in all.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Absolute path of a file or folder, URL-encoded.

200.description: A file's bytes, or a folder's listing (paths relative to the folder, `/`-separated).

400.description: Not an absolute local path, not a model, texture or weather file, or over the limits.

path.value: error: path must be an absolute local path such as C:\models\house.usdz (no network or device paths)

type.value: error: not a model, texture or weather file (.usd .usda .usdc .usdz .glb .gltf .obj .mtl .bin .png .jpg .jpeg .webp .exr .hdr .epw)

size.value: error: C:\models holds over 2000 model files or 2048 MB: open a subfolder or single files

404.description: No such file or folder, or agent routes are off.

path.value: error: no such file or folder: C:\models\house.usdz

get.description: The reports stored with `saveReport`, each spec as a JSON string (parsed one by one, so a damaged file cannot break the list) and whether a PDF exists, from `<cache>/reports/<id>/`: `report.json`, `index.html` (the page last printed) and `report.pdf`. Agents use the report tools.

put.description: Creates or replaces the report's `report.json` with the body (at most 1 MB): a `ReportSpec`, stored as it comes (written to a temporary file and renamed, so a crash never leaves half a spec).

example.title: Sun on the south facade
example.summary: On 21 March the south facade gets 0.754 h of sun on average.

blocks.text: The neighbour to the south shades it from 10:00.

delete.description: Removes the report's folder: spec, page and PDF. A program that holds `report.pdf` open (a PDF viewer that locks it) makes it refuse and the report stays: close the PDF and delete again.

404.description: No such report, or agent routes are off.

409.description: The PDF is open in another program, or the report is printing.

post.summary: Print a report page to PDF (app)
post.description: Saves the body, the report page the app rendered (self-contained HTML in the kit-report layout), as `index.html` behind a Content-Security-Policy that loads nothing but inline styles and `data:` images and fonts, and prints it to `report.pdf` with headless Chrome or Edge (`--browser PATH`, else the registered one), one print at a time, within 30 s. Answers the PDF's path and URL (`getReportPdf`), pages, bytes and embedded fonts; `fallback` lists those that are not kit-ui's, i.e. characters drawn with a system font.

text/html.example:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en" data-kit="sim" data-theme="light" data-density="compact">
<head><meta charset="utf-8"><style>/* kit-ui.css, its fonts as data URIs */</style></head>
<body><main class="report stack" id="main">...</main></body></html>

400.description: The page carries an `http-equiv` tag: a refresh would send the print to another file.

404.description: No such report (store its spec first), or agent routes are off.

409.description: `report.pdf` is open in another program (a PDF viewer that locks it); the old PDF stays.

500.description: No browser to print with, or it printed no PDF (it failed, or took over 30 s).

browser.value: error: no Chrome or Edge found to print the PDF: start daylight_server with --browser PATH

print.value: error: the browser printed no PDF (no PDF within 30 s): C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe

get.description: The PDF last printed by `printReport` (its `url` points here), inline so the browser shows it, never cached. Like every route of this tag it answers only on this machine.

404.description: No PDF yet, or agent routes are off.

get.description: With no app tab open, the agent works in the app hidden in headless Chrome (`--web` or `--app-url`), which records here, in memory, its `settings` (`epw`: a weather file opened by path), `subdiv` and `subdivOverride`, the state-changing tool calls it made (`steps`) and whether it ran (`ran`). An app tab opening later replays the record and deletes it (`deleteSession`), which ends the hidden instance.

200.description: The record, as the hidden instance stored it.

204.description: No session: no hidden instance, or picked up already (not an error, so an app tab's console stays clean).

put.description: Replaces the record with the body, one JSON object (the hidden instance sends it after each change). It stays in memory until `deleteSession` or the server exits.

delete.description: Forgets the record and ends the hidden instance (its browser and every process it started). Sent by the app tab that picked the session up.

MeshId.name: id
MeshId.description: Mesh id chosen by the client, 1 to 64 of `[A-Za-z0-9-]`: a UUID, or a content id as the bindings make it (the SHA-256 hex of the bytes; with `?name=`, sha256(hex + "\0name\0" + name)), shared by every client that sends the same mesh.

Inline.name: inline
Inline.description: `1`: a `done` job also carries its values inline as `values_b64` (up to 4,194,304 values).

ClientId.name: X-Client-Id
ClientId.description: Identifies one client (a browser tab, a script) for the per-client job limit and `listMyJobs`. Without it the network address is used.

TabId.name: X-Client-Id
TabId.description: This page load's id, a random UUID per load (a duplicated tab is another tab).

ReportId.name: id
ReportId.description: Report id chosen by the app: 1 to 64 of `[a-z0-9-]` (lowercase: report folders ignore case on Windows).

SetId.name: id
SetId.description: Set id chosen by the app: 1 to 64 of `[a-z0-9-]` (lowercase: file names ignore case on Windows).

RunRequest.description: One run: meshes by id, CLI flags, weather.

BadRequest.description: Invalid request: unknown flag, bad id, unusable weather, ... The text starts with `error: <cause>`; flag errors append the CLI usage.

Missing.description: The server does not hold these meshes (never uploaded, or evicted): `PUT /mesh/{id}` each and submit again.

TooLarge.description: The result would hold more than 134,217,728 values (rows = sensor faces or points, columns = quantities x sides; views: its columns x sides), more than a browser can take in one piece. Nothing is queued.

text/plain.example: error: 17244108 rows x 12 columns = 206929296 values, over the 134217728 one run can return; pick fewer quantities, one side or fewer receivers

TooManyJobs.description: This client already has its limit of jobs queued or running.

DownloadFailed.description: The weather resource could not be downloaded.

NoSuchJob.description: Unknown id, or finished more than 15 minutes ago.

Forbidden.description: Agent routes answer only requests from this machine: TCP peer 127.0.0.1 or ::1, `Host` localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1] (any port), `Origin` absent or the page's own, `Sec-Fetch-Site` absent, `none` or `same-origin`, no `Forwarded`, `X-Forwarded-*`, `X-Real-IP` or `Via` header (a proxy), and the JSON bodies of `mcpMessage` and `bridgeResult` sent as `Content-Type: application/json`.

text/plain.example: error: agent routes answer only on this machine (Host localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1]; same origin; no proxy; JSON bodies as Content-Type: application/json)

NotEnabled.description: The server runs without `--mcp`, so every agent route is off.

text/plain.example: error: agent routes are off (start daylight_server with --mcp)

NotObject.description: The body is not one JSON object.

text/plain.example: error: the body is one JSON object (the set)

NotStored.description: The file could not be written or removed (disk full, no access, held open).

ErrorText.description: A plain-text error: the first line `error: <cause>`; a usage error appends the CLI usage (`getUsage`).

sensors.description: Ids of the receiving meshes (analysed; they also cast shade unless `--no-self-occlude`, or `--no-occlude` names them). Rows of the result follow this order.

context.description: Ids of meshes that only cast shade (views: only block rays, or are `--target`s).

tool.description: Which CLI runs: `daylight` (sun and sky) or `views` (what each element sees; no weather).

args.description: The tool's CLI flags, one array element per token (`["--quantity", "radiation,sunhours"]`). `GET /usage/{tool}` lists every flag with its default; [daylight.md](https://github.com/Cybernaut0815/kit-sim_core/blob/main/docs/daylight.md) and [views.md](https://github.com/Cybernaut0815/kit-sim_core/blob/main/docs/views.md) explain them. Daylight needs weather for every quantity but `sunhours` (`epw`, `epw_url`, or `--clear-sky` with `--lat` and `--lon`); views takes none. Refused over HTTP: mesh paths, `--context FILE`, `--epw FILE` (send `epw` or `epw_url`), `--out`, `--timeseries`, `--dump-*`, `--bench`. A bad flag or value is a `400` at submission; names in `--optics`, `--no-occlude` and `--target` (a mesh's `?name=`, made unique per run) resolve against the run's meshes when it runs.

epw.description: An hourly EPW weather file (8760 or 8784 rows). Give this, `epw_url` or `--clear-sky`, at most one; none with `tool` views.

epw_url.description: An allowed weather URL (see `proxyDownload`); the server downloads it once and caches it.

first.description: First row of this mesh in `values_b64`.

count.description: Rows of this mesh: its faces, or its points with `--on vertices`.

response.description: `hit`: an identical request was answered from the result cache, nothing ran.

scene.description: `reused`: the scene was still on the GPU, so its acceleration structure was not rebuilt; `built`: built for this run, then kept like the others (`--gpu-scenes`). A scene is the `sensors` then `context` ids in order, `--no-self-occlude`, the `--no-occlude` set and the layout of the slots that cast shade (which transmit; with `--bounces`, whether their RHO or glass differ). New `--optics` values and `--fresnel` reuse a scene while that layout stays; a slot that starts or stops transmitting, or `--bounces` switched on or off over slots that differ, is another scene.

weather.description: `hit`: the parsed weather was cached; `none`: no weather file (clear sky or sun hours).

RunResult.description: A finished run: the CLI's output manifest, the values, and the server's timings and cache report.

ResultFields.description: The result fields; all present on a `RunResult` and on a `done` job.

columns.description: Column names `<quantity>_<side>`, in `--quantity` order, sides inner (views: `<name>_<side>`, listed in `/usage/views`).

duration_h.description: Daylight: hours represented by the evaluated steps.

dirs.description: Daylight: ray directions traced per sensor.

view.description: Views: the field as run: `fov` [H, LO, HI], `gaze` (`level`, only with `--gaze level` and H < 360), `cell`, `grid` [rows, columns], `jitter`, `north`, `offset`, `far`, `near` (the 0.1 m floor), `virtual_ground`, `ground_z` (the plane's height), `transmission` (only when on), `reach`, `classes` and `image` (the ray order).

meshes.description: Receiving meshes in `sensors` order with their row ranges.

values_b64.description: float64 little-endian, row-major `[sum(meshes.count) x columns.length]`, the float32 values widened. Always in a `POST /run` answer; on a job only with `inline=1` and up to 4,194,304 values (else read `getJobValues`).

timing.description: Where `run_s` went, in ms: host prep (triangles, sensors), sky (sun, sky model, weights), build (upload + acceleration structure), reduce (sums, downloads included), and the GPU's own trace and bounce time; `totalMs` = run_s.

gpu.description: What the GPU did in this run: sensor x direction slots traced (hemisphere-culled ones included), kernel launches, acceleration-structure bytes.

values.description: Where the values are (`getJobValues`): float32 little-endian, column-major.

run_s.description: Seconds the GPU worker spent on this run.

total_s.description: Seconds from submission to the result (queue wait included).

JobState.description: `queued` waits for the GPU, `running` is on it; the other three are final.

position.description: Jobs ahead of this one, the running job included; 0 while running or finished.

status.description: `error`: the HTTP status `runSync` would answer (507 out of memory, 500 runtime, also an `--optics` row the run's meshes do not resolve, a `--no-occlude` NAME that is unknown, ambiguous or a context mesh, or a views `--target` NAME the meshes do not resolve); `cancelled`: 409.

progress.description: `running`: the share of sensors traced so far (the long poll answers within 2 s while a job runs).

eta_s.description: `running`: seconds left at the pace so far, once `progress` > 0.

Job.description: A job; when `state` is `done` it also carries every `RunResult` field.

jobs_retained.description: Jobs in memory, finished ones included.

agents.description: Whether this request may use the agent routes (`--mcp`, and it comes from this machine): the web app starts its side of them only then.

JsonRpcRequest.description: One JSON-RPC 2.0 request, or a notification (no `id`).

id.description: Echoed in the answer exactly as sent.

JsonRpcResponse.description: The answer to one request: its `result`, or an `error`.

id.description: The request's `id`; `null` when the request could not be read.

CallToolResult.description: An MCP tool result as the app answers it: text (compact JSON or a message; a URL such as a report PDF's comes inside it) and images (JPEG, base64); `isError` when the step could not be done, its text saying what to fix.

spec.description: `report.json` as stored, as a string: parse it.
`<id>.json` as stored, as a string: parse it.

pdf.description: Absolute path of `report.pdf` on this machine.

url.description: Where `getReportPdf` serves it, on the address the request came to.

fonts.description: PostScript names of the embedded fonts, subset tags dropped.

fallback.description: The fonts that are not kit-ui's (Geist, Geist Mono, Space Mono, Tektur): the browser drew some characters with a system font. Empty for a clean report.

Id.description: A set's or report's id: the name's slug and a random suffix (`facade-sun-k3f9`).

Look.description: A quantity's colours as the Results panel sets them: `gradient` (a built-in or library name), `scaling`, the legend domain `min`/`max` and the problem range `lo`/`hi` (null: open).

AnalysisSet.description: One analysis' whole setup, as the web app saves it (`web/src/sets/apply.ts`). Opening it applies each model entry to its own model only (same letter and file); another model takes it only as a copy. The app checks it; the server stores it as it comes.

roles.description: Receivers and shades by USD prim path; paths not listed are none.

shade.description: A receiver that casts no shade.

optics.description: Materials edits by material path, plus the default and glass rows.

settings.description: Daylight: `{sim, time}`; views: `{viewSim}`, as the app's settings name them.

weather.description: Daylight: the source, station or EPW file name, turbidity and altitude.

looks.description: `quantities`: each quantity's `Look`; `colors`: the problem range's two colours.

subdiv.description: The subdivision level it runs at (-1 auto, 0 off).

subdivOverride.description: That level also for the meshes with their own refinement (absent: the app's setting).

CombinedView.description: Saved sets' results weighed into one value per element, the Combined tab's (`web/src/sets/model.ts`).

unit.description: The combined value's unit ('': a score).

column.description: A column of that set's result.

fn.description: The transfer applied first; `lo` and `hi` are its bounds.

meshes.description: Only the receivers at or under these prim paths (absent: all).

SavedSet.description: What `/sets` stores: an analysis set or a combined view.

ReportSpec.description: A report as the web app saves it (`web/src/report/spec.ts`): the models and the run each had at save time, statistics, a summary and blocks. The app checks it; the server stores it as it comes.

variants.description: Prim path -> variant set -> the variant chosen (the file's own are not listed).

runKey.description: The run's settings, so a later generation can tell whether the results are still those the text was written on.

ranges.description: Per quantity shown, its problem range `{lo, hi}` at save.

blocks.description: `text` {title?, text}, `chart` {chart, caption}, `view` {name, view, column, caption, section?}, `table` {column, by?, parts?, metrics, caption}.

chart.description: As `update_settings` takes a chart, models as letters.

saved.description: The chart as saved (the app's Reset).
